events.summary: CEO William Brennan and CFO Daniel Fleming each filed a Form 4 (accepted about 21:25 ET). Both show only code F transactions: shares the company withheld to pay income tax when restricted stock units (RSUs) vested, with the footnote 'Represents shares withheld by the Issuer to satisfy tax withholding obligations in connection with the vesting and settlement of RSUs.' events.type: insider sales outside 10b5-1 plans (older filings newly identified; context for the thesis breaker)
events.summary: Reading every Credo Form 4 back to June (raw SEC XML) shows that the pipeline's 10-day filings window understated the non-plan selling. Open-market sales with the 10b5-1 box NOT checked, and with no plan adoption date on the matching Form 144: (1) CTO and director Chi Fung (Lawrence) Cheng sold 3,790 shares at $170.00 on 2026-09-04 (about $0.64m; shares from an RSU vest on 2025-09-01; about 2.7% of his directly held shares; he also holds about 5.7m shares through a family trust that sells under a separate plan); (2) Chief Legal Officer James Laufman sold 5,000 shares at $185.00 on 2026-09-21 (about $0.93m) and (3) 5,000 shares at $205.00 on 2026-10-01 (about $1.03m; already in the log). Earlier in the year: Laufman 5,000 shares at $264.485 on 2026-06-11 and director Clyde Hosein 3,451 shares at $262.325 on 2026-07-01, both without the plan box. So over about four weeks (4 Sept to 1 Oct) TWO insiders sold outside plans, about $2.59m in total, against about $53.1m of pre-planned sales by the CEO (plan adopted 2026-06-10), CTO (plan adopted 2025-09-05) and COO in the same period. Round-number prices ($170, $185, $205) and fixed 5,000-share lots look like limit orders on newly vested stock (inference, medium). No new non-plan sale was filed in this window.
events.why_it_matters: Santi's breaker is 'several insiders sold on the open market outside pre-planned 10b5-1 plans'. Two people over four weeks, small amounts and small fractions of their holdings: borderline under the word 'several' (see thesis_breaker_checks). The previous report's statement that Laufman was the only non-plan seller was true only for the pipeline's 10-day window.

products.name: Active electrical cables (AECs, branded ZeroFlap AECs) - background only, no product news in the window
products.what_it_is: Copper cables with a small signal-cleaning chip in each end that link servers and switches a few metres apart inside AI data centers.
products.analogy: A garden hose with a booster pump at each end: plain copper loses 'pressure' (signal) over distance; the chips restore it.
products.buyers: Hyperscale cloud companies and AI cloud providers; Credo does not name them. Four customers were 84% of Q1 FY2027 revenue (33/28/13/10%).
products.how_it_works: Credo designs the chips and sells the finished cable; over a few metres it is cheaper and uses less power than an optical link.
products.sales: Not disclosed separately. Proxy (labelled): total company revenue $479.0m in Q1 FY2027 (+114.7%), with AECs described by management as the largest business; optical products guided above $600m for fiscal 2027 (call transcript, tier 3).
products.stage: Shipping in volume; 1.6T optical transceivers (224G per lane) added to the ZeroFlap family on 2026-09-15 (announced, shipping status not stated in this research).
products.size_for_company: Largest product line (exact share not disclosed).
products.competition: Marvell (Alaska AECs, 'Golden Cable' partner programme with cable makers such as Amphenol) and Astera Labs (Taurus AEC chips), per tier-3 coverage; longer term, optics replacing copper.
products.why_investors_care: It is the engine of the 100%+ growth; the thesis depends on top customers keeping it in new designs.
products.watch_next: Q2 FY2027 results (estimated about 2026-12-02): revenue vs $525-535m guide, customer shares, any optical revenue figure.
